content.content:
1	# 08 — Global-e (International Checkout)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Global-e is the international checkout owner for Zimmermann. When the shopper's destination is outside the domestic market of the active storefront, the PWA hands the cart to a Global-e-hosted checkout embedded as an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route.
6	
7	PWA responsibilities:
8	
9	- Reading target-currency prices from SFCC price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart
10	- Showing DDP/DDU duties messaging
11	- Assembling and triggering the cart handoff
12	- Embedding the Global-e checkout iframe
13	- Handling the order-completion return path
14	
15	Server-side flows (nightly Global-e → SFCC price feed, daily SFCC → Global-e catalogue export, GiveX webhooks, and the post-order Global-e → SFCC webhook) are **outside** the PWA layer.
16	
17	## 2. Checkout ownership matrix
18	
19	| Storefront                                               | Destination                                                                                                | Checkout                                                                       |
20	| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
21	| AU (root)                                                | AU + Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands)                                                          | SFCC (REG-003). Avalara duties for NZ and New Caledonia; other Oceania is DDU. |
22	| US (`/us/`)                                              | US + Puerto Rico                                                                                           | SFCC (REG-005)                                                                 |
23	| US (`/en-ca/`, same SFCC site)                           | Canada, Mexico, all other Americas                                                                         | Global-e (REG-005, branched by shipping address)                               |
24	| UK (`/uk/`)                                              | UK only                                                                                                    | SFCC (REG-004)                                                                 |
25	| EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`) | EU domestic countries                                                                                      | SFCC (REG-006 dom)                                                             |
26	| EU international (`/en-ch/`)                             | Non-EU Europe + Africa + remainder                                                                         | Global-e (REG-006 intl)                                                        |
27	| HK (`/hk/`)                                              | HK + East, South, Southeast, and Central Asia (incl. China, Japan, India, Singapore) + Australia (REG-027) | Global-e (REG-007)                                                             |
28	| ME (`/en-ae/`)                                           | UAE + GCC + Levant + Egypt + Israel                                                                        | Global-e (REG-008)                                                             |
29	
30	Checkout ownership branches at PDP and cart, not only at the checkout page.
31	
32	> Non-Oceania shoppers who select "Australia" in the country selector are routed to the HK storefront (REG-027), not the geo-gated AU site.
33	
34	## 3. Browser-side architecture
35	
36	```
37	Shopper on a Global-e-served storefront (or chooses an international destination)
38	        │
39	        ▼
40	PDP / PLP / cart read the target-currency price from the SFCC Global-e-derived
41	price books (calculated by the nightly feed) and format it per locale
42	        │
43	        ▼
44	Add to cart — basket persists in SFCC in storefront currency
45	        │
46	        ▼
47	Checkout CTA — PWA calls SFCC to assemble the complete cart payload in the
48	shopper's target currency (per PRC-34..42)
49	        │
50	        ▼
51	SFCC posts the cart to Global-e (server-side) — "SendCart" — and returns a
52	`cartToken` representing the cloned cart on Global-e's side. SFCC also calls
53	`basket.reserveInventory()` before the SendCart request (default hold: 30 min).
54	        │
55	        ▼
56	PWA renders a Zimmermann checkout route that embeds the Global-e checkout
57	inside an iframe using the `cartToken`. The shopper remains on www.zimmermann.com
58	(parent frame); the iframe loads from Global-e's checkout origin.
59	        │
60	        ▼
61	Inside the iframe Global-e collects shipping address, payment, duties, and tax.
62	When the shopper clicks "Place Order", Global-e calls the SFCC
63	`Globale-ValidateCart` endpoint to check stock against SFCC inventory.
64	If stock is insufficient the shopper sees a popup and is redirected to cart —
65	no order is created on either side.
66	        │
67	        ▼
68	After validation passes, Global-e sends a `postMessage` to the parent frame.
69	The parent frame makes an AJAX request to SFCC `orderCreate()`, which converts
70	the basket to an SFCC order with status **Created**. If this call fails (session
71	expiry, stock change) Global-e's retry mechanism falls back to the
72	`SendOrderToMerchant` path to recreate and place the order.
73	        │
74	        ▼
75	Global-e calls SFCC's `SendOrderToMerchant` endpoint seconds later to enrich
76	the order with full international transaction data. Order status → **New**.
77	        │
78	        ▼
79	After fraud screening passes, Global-e calls SFCC's `PerformPayment` endpoint.
80	Payment status → **Paid**; export status → **Ready for Export**.
81	        │
82	        ▼
83	Order completion: the PWA navigates the parent frame to the Zimmermann
84	confirmation route, fetches the order from SFCC, and renders the confirmation.
85	The order number shown to shoppers is the Global-e order number
86	(format: `GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`); SFCC domestic orders
87	continue to show the SFCC order number.
88	```
89	
90	- **Pre-checkout currency display.** Target-currency prices are read from the SFCC Global-e-derived price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart.
91	  SFCC holds these price books, regenerated nightly from Global-e's FX, coefficient, and rounding feed (PRC-34, PRC-38..40).
92	  Calculated prices are also in the SFCC search index so price filters and sort work on PLP and search results (PRC-41).
93	  The PWA does not convert prices client-side — it formats the SFCC-supplied target-currency price per locale (symbol position, decimal places including zero-decimal currencies, thousand separator) per PRC-47.
94	  HK and ME follow the same pattern: prices are read from HKD and AED SFCC price books, not from a Global-e client-side widget.
95	  No Global-e client-side script is needed to display pricing.
96	
97	- **DDP/DDU duties messaging.** Shown on PDP per destination country, configurable per country (PRC-15). The data source for this flag (SFCC product attribute vs. Global-e price book field) is not specified in the PRDs — confirm with the integration team before implementing.
98	
99	- **Handoff payload.** SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency at handoff — line items, quantities, target-currency prices, applied promotions, coupons, Retail Rewards, and gift cards (PRC-16).
100	  Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from the iframe onwards.
101	
102	- **Iframe embed.** The Global-e checkout renders inside an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route. The `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` directive must list the Global-e checkout origin (see §9 item 1). Iframe height is managed via Global-e's `postMessage` contract.
103	
104	- **Shipping country lock.** The shipping country is determined by the country selector pre-checkout and cannot be changed inside the Global-e iframe (REG-028).
105	
106	- **Return path.** On order completion Global-e signals the parent frame via `postMessage`.
107	  The `postMessage` triggers an AJAX call from the parent frame to SFCC `orderCreate()` (see the flow diagram above for the full sequence).
108	  The PWA's `window` `"message"` event listener must enforce three conditions before acting on any message:
109	  1. **`event.origin`** matches the confirmed Global-e checkout origin (see §9 item 1).
110	  2. **`event.source`** equals the checkout `<iframe>` element's `contentWindow` — prevents other windows on the same trusted origin from triggering order completion.
111	  3. **Message schema** matches the expected Global-e payload shape — reject and ignore any message that does not conform.
112	  After all three checks pass:
113	  - Validate `orderRef` from the payload matches the expected Global-e format (`GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`) before using it. Reject and ignore the message if it does not match.
114	  - Construct the confirmation URL using `URLSearchParams` (or equivalent URL-safe encoding) rather than direct string interpolation — e.g. `new URLSearchParams({ orderRef }).toString()` — to prevent injection via a malformed payload value.
115	  - Navigate the parent frame to `/{prefix}/checkout/confirmation?<encoded-params>` and render the confirmation from the SFCC order record.
116	  The international order confirmation email is sent by Global-e; the PWA owns only the on-page confirmation display (CFD-071).
117	
118	## 4. Authentication and credentials
119	
120	| Credential                         | Where used                                                     | Sensitivity                        |
121	| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
122	| Global-e Merchant ID               | Embedded in handoff request                                    | Public                             |
123	| Global-e API key and shared secret | Server-side only (SFCC → Global-e and Global-e webhook → SFCC) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
124	
125	## 5. Data exchanged
126	
127	**Browser / iframe → Global-e (client-side inputs):**
128	
129	- Shopper IP and device user agent (passed by the browser)
130	- Pre-selected destination country (locked once inside the iframe)
131	- Order reference for return-webhook correlation
132	
133	**SFCC → Global-e (SendCart server-side payload):**
134	
135	- Cart line items (SKU, quantity, target-currency price)
136	- Guest email (via `globale.getGuestEmail` hook — pre-populates shopper email in the iframe)
137	- Saved addresses for logged-in shoppers (via `globale.getCustomerAddresses`)
138	- Didomi consent state mapped to Global-e's 0/1/2 scale (via `globale.getCookieConsent`)
139	- Marketing opt-in and direct communication consent flags (via `globale.getAllowMailsFromMerchant` / `globale.getAllowDirectCommunicationFromMerchant`)
140	
141	**Global-e → Browser (return):** `postMessage` event to the parent frame triggering `orderCreate()`, after which the parent navigates to the Zimmermann confirmation route.
142	
143	**Runtime session data available to the PWA:**
144	
145	Global-e writes these SFCC session custom attributes on every storefront request after initialisation.
146	The PWA can read these from the SFCC session to determine country/currency context before handoff.
147	
148	| Attribute         | Type    | Description                                  | Example |
149	| ----------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------- |
150	| `geCountry`       | String  | Currently selected/detected country (ISO2)   | `GB`    |
151	| `geIsOperated`    | Boolean | Whether this country is operated by Global-e | `true`  |
152	| `geCurrency`      | String  | Currency ISO3 for the selected country       | `GBP`   |
153	| `gePriceStrategy` | String  | Pricing strategy (`DYNAMIC` or `FIXED`)      | `FIXED` |
154	
155	Global-e also sets a `GlobalE_Data` cookie (available client-side) with four fields that map to session attributes:
156	`countryISO` → `geCountry`, `cultureCode` → `geCulture`, `currencyCode` → `geCurrency`, `apiVersion` → `geApiVersion`.
157	Note that `geCulture` and `geApiVersion` are session attributes written by Global-e but are not listed in the table above — they are only surfaced via the cookie.
158	
159	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
160	
161	- Pre-checkout prices come from standard SFCC product/price API responses. No extra Global-e network request sits on the PDP or PLP critical path.
162	- The handoff route embeds the Global-e iframe post-interaction; iframe load latency does not affect parent-page LCP.
163	- Emit `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Global-e checkout origin from the cart page to warm the TLS handshake before the iframe loads.
164	- Any retained Global-e client-side script (e.g. duties messaging) must be deferred and load after LCP.
165	- The Global-e team must configure `frame-ancestors` / `X-Frame-Options` to permit embedding under `www.zimmermann.com`.
166	
167	## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation
168	
169	| Failure                                                                    | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
170	| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
171	| SFCC Global-e-derived price book is missing or stale for a target currency | Show the storefront-currency price with the message "Final pricing in your currency shown at checkout." Do not silently fall back to an SFCC checkout for an international destination — that would route the order through the wrong checkout flow and carries tax / regulatory risk. |
172	| Handoff fails (Global-e API outage at cart → handoff)                      | Surface a hard error: "International checkout is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly." Do not place the order in SFCC.                                                                                                                                                   |
173	| Return webhook from Global-e to SFCC is delayed                            | Render the confirmation with the order reference and a "Your order is being processed" state. Full details render once SFCC receives the order.                                                                                                                                        |
174	| Cart total mismatch between SFCC and Global-e at handoff                   | Reject the order; surface a hard error. Never silently adjust totals.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
175	
176	## 8. Security
177	
178	- The Global-e checkout domain is third-party. Cross-site cookies do not propagate — cart context is passed inside the handoff payload, not via cookies.
179	- The `postMessage` listener in the parent frame must enforce all three checks documented in §3 — `event.origin`, `event.source`, and message schema — plus `orderRef` format validation and URL-safe query encoding before constructing the confirmation URL. See §3 "Return path" for the full requirements.
180	
181	## 9. Open items
182	
183	1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply:
184	
185	   - The `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers.
186	   - The `postMessage` trusted sender origin — the vendor guide confirms that the Global-e iframe sends a `postMessage` to the parent frame to trigger `orderCreate()`, but does not specify the exact origin string or the full message schema. The `event.origin` value and message payload shape must be obtained from Global-e directly before the listener can be safely implemented.
187	     Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.
188	
189	2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order (from SFCC), to decide between full order detail and a "View on tracking page" fallback.
190	   Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.

# 08 — Global-e (International Checkout)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Global-e is the international checkout owner for Zimmermann. When the shopper's destination is outside the domestic market of the active storefront, the PWA hands the cart to a Global-e-hosted checkout embedded as an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route.

PWA responsibilities:

- Reading target-currency prices from SFCC price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart
- Showing DDP/DDU duties messaging
- Assembling and triggering the cart handoff
- Embedding the Global-e checkout iframe
- Handling the order-completion return path

Server-side flows (nightly Global-e → SFCC price feed, daily SFCC → Global-e catalogue export, GiveX webhooks, and the post-order Global-e → SFCC webhook) are **outside** the PWA layer.

## 2. Checkout ownership matrix

| Storefront                                               | Destination                                                                                                | Checkout                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| AU (root)                                                | AU + Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands)                                                          | SFCC (REG-003). Avalara duties for NZ and New Caledonia; other Oceania is DDU. |
| US (`/us/`)                                              | US + Puerto Rico                                                                                           | SFCC (REG-005)                                                                 |
| US (`/en-ca/`, same SFCC site)                           | Canada, Mexico, all other Americas                                                                         | Global-e (REG-005, branched by shipping address)                               |
| UK (`/uk/`)                                              | UK only                                                                                                    | SFCC (REG-004)                                                                 |
| EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`) | EU domestic countries                                                                                      | SFCC (REG-006 dom)                                                             |
| EU international (`/en-ch/`)                             | Non-EU Europe + Africa + remainder                                                                         | Global-e (REG-006 intl)                                                        |
| HK (`/hk/`)                                              | HK + East, South, Southeast, and Central Asia (incl. China, Japan, India, Singapore) + Australia (REG-027) | Global-e (REG-007)                                                             |
| ME (`/en-ae/`)                                           | UAE + GCC + Levant + Egypt + Israel                                                                        | Global-e (REG-008)                                                             |

Checkout ownership branches at PDP and cart, not only at the checkout page.

> Non-Oceania shoppers who select "Australia" in the country selector are routed to the HK storefront (REG-027), not the geo-gated AU site.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
Shopper on a Global-e-served storefront (or chooses an international destination)
        │
        ▼
PDP / PLP / cart read the target-currency price from the SFCC Global-e-derived
price books (calculated by the nightly feed) and format it per locale
        │
        ▼
Add to cart — basket persists in SFCC in storefront currency
        │
        ▼
Checkout CTA — PWA calls SFCC to assemble the complete cart payload in the
shopper's target currency (per PRC-34..42)
        │
        ▼
SFCC posts the cart to Global-e (server-side) — "SendCart" — and returns a
`cartToken` representing the cloned cart on Global-e's side. SFCC also calls
`basket.reserveInventory()` before the SendCart request (default hold: 30 min).
        │
        ▼
PWA renders a Zimmermann checkout route that embeds the Global-e checkout
inside an iframe using the `cartToken`. The shopper remains on www.zimmermann.com
(parent frame); the iframe loads from Global-e's checkout origin.
        │
        ▼
Inside the iframe Global-e collects shipping address, payment, duties, and tax.
When the shopper clicks "Place Order", Global-e calls the SFCC
`Globale-ValidateCart` endpoint to check stock against SFCC inventory.
If stock is insufficient the shopper sees a popup and is redirected to cart —
no order is created on either side.
        │
        ▼
After validation passes, Global-e sends a `postMessage` to the parent frame.
The parent frame makes an AJAX request to SFCC `orderCreate()`, which converts
the basket to an SFCC order with status **Created**. If this call fails (session
expiry, stock change) Global-e's retry mechanism falls back to the
`SendOrderToMerchant` path to recreate and place the order.
        │
        ▼
Global-e calls SFCC's `SendOrderToMerchant` endpoint seconds later to enrich
the order with full international transaction data. Order status → **New**.
        │
        ▼
After fraud screening passes, Global-e calls SFCC's `PerformPayment` endpoint.
Payment status → **Paid**; export status → **Ready for Export**.
        │
        ▼
Order completion: the PWA navigates the parent frame to the Zimmermann
confirmation route, fetches the order from SFCC, and renders the confirmation.
The order number shown to shoppers is the Global-e order number
(format: `GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`); SFCC domestic orders
continue to show the SFCC order number.
```

- **Pre-checkout currency display.** Target-currency prices are read from the SFCC Global-e-derived price books on PDP, PLP, cart, and mini-cart.
  SFCC holds these price books, regenerated nightly from Global-e's FX, coefficient, and rounding feed (PRC-34, PRC-38..40).
  Calculated prices are also in the SFCC search index so price filters and sort work on PLP and search results (PRC-41).
  The PWA does not convert prices client-side — it formats the SFCC-supplied target-currency price per locale (symbol position, decimal places including zero-decimal currencies, thousand separator) per PRC-47.
  HK and ME follow the same pattern: prices are read from HKD and AED SFCC price books, not from a Global-e client-side widget.
  No Global-e client-side script is needed to display pricing.

- **DDP/DDU duties messaging.** Shown on PDP per destination country, configurable per country (PRC-15). The data source for this flag (SFCC product attribute vs. Global-e price book field) is not specified in the PRDs — confirm with the integration team before implementing.

- **Handoff payload.** SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency at handoff — line items, quantities, target-currency prices, applied promotions, coupons, Retail Rewards, and gift cards (PRC-16).
  Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from the iframe onwards.

- **Iframe embed.** The Global-e checkout renders inside an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route. The `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` directive must list the Global-e checkout origin (see §9 item 1). Iframe height is managed via Global-e's `postMessage` contract.

- **Shipping country lock.** The shipping country is determined by the country selector pre-checkout and cannot be changed inside the Global-e iframe (REG-028).

- **Return path.** On order completion Global-e signals the parent frame via `postMessage`.
  The `postMessage` triggers an AJAX call from the parent frame to SFCC `orderCreate()` (see the flow diagram above for the full sequence).
  The PWA's `window` `"message"` event listener must enforce three conditions before acting on any message:
  1. **`event.origin`** matches the confirmed Global-e checkout origin (see §9 item 1).
  2. **`event.source`** equals the checkout `<iframe>` element's `contentWindow` — prevents other windows on the same trusted origin from triggering order completion.
  3. **Message schema** matches the expected Global-e payload shape — reject and ignore any message that does not conform.
  After all three checks pass:
  - Validate `orderRef` from the payload matches the expected Global-e format (`GE<digits><country>`, e.g. `GE111326998GB`) before using it. Reject and ignore the message if it does not match.
  - Construct the confirmation URL using `URLSearchParams` (or equivalent URL-safe encoding) rather than direct string interpolation — e.g. `new URLSearchParams({ orderRef }).toString()` — to prevent injection via a malformed payload value.
  - Navigate the parent frame to `/{prefix}/checkout/confirmation?<encoded-params>` and render the confirmation from the SFCC order record.
  The international order confirmation email is sent by Global-e; the PWA owns only the on-page confirmation display (CFD-071).

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Credential                         | Where used                                                     | Sensitivity                        |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Global-e Merchant ID               | Embedded in handoff request                                    | Public                             |
| Global-e API key and shared secret | Server-side only (SFCC → Global-e and Global-e webhook → SFCC) | Secret — never reaches the browser |

## 5. Data exchanged

**Browser / iframe → Global-e (client-side inputs):**

- Shopper IP and device user agent (passed by the browser)
- Pre-selected destination country (locked once inside the iframe)
- Order reference for return-webhook correlation

**SFCC → Global-e (SendCart server-side payload):**

- Cart line items (SKU, quantity, target-currency price)
- Guest email (via `globale.getGuestEmail` hook — pre-populates shopper email in the iframe)
- Saved addresses for logged-in shoppers (via `globale.getCustomerAddresses`)
- Didomi consent state mapped to Global-e's 0/1/2 scale (via `globale.getCookieConsent`)
- Marketing opt-in and direct communication consent flags (via `globale.getAllowMailsFromMerchant` / `globale.getAllowDirectCommunicationFromMerchant`)

**Global-e → Browser (return):** `postMessage` event to the parent frame triggering `orderCreate()`, after which the parent navigates to the Zimmermann confirmation route.

**Runtime session data available to the PWA:**

Global-e writes these SFCC session custom attributes on every storefront request after initialisation.
The PWA can read these from the SFCC session to determine country/currency context before handoff.

| Attribute         | Type    | Description                                  | Example |
| ----------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `geCountry`       | String  | Currently selected/detected country (ISO2)   | `GB`    |
| `geIsOperated`    | Boolean | Whether this country is operated by Global-e | `true`  |
| `geCurrency`      | String  | Currency ISO3 for the selected country       | `GBP`   |
| `gePriceStrategy` | String  | Pricing strategy (`DYNAMIC` or `FIXED`)      | `FIXED` |

Global-e also sets a `GlobalE_Data` cookie (available client-side) with four fields that map to session attributes:
`countryISO` → `geCountry`, `cultureCode` → `geCulture`, `currencyCode` → `geCurrency`, `apiVersion` → `geApiVersion`.
Note that `geCulture` and `geApiVersion` are session attributes written by Global-e but are not listed in the table above — they are only surfaced via the cookie.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- Pre-checkout prices come from standard SFCC product/price API responses. No extra Global-e network request sits on the PDP or PLP critical path.
- The handoff route embeds the Global-e iframe post-interaction; iframe load latency does not affect parent-page LCP.
- Emit `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Global-e checkout origin from the cart page to warm the TLS handshake before the iframe loads.
- Any retained Global-e client-side script (e.g. duties messaging) must be deferred and load after LCP.
- The Global-e team must configure `frame-ancestors` / `X-Frame-Options` to permit embedding under `www.zimmermann.com`.

## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure                                                                    | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SFCC Global-e-derived price book is missing or stale for a target currency | Show the storefront-currency price with the message "Final pricing in your currency shown at checkout." Do not silently fall back to an SFCC checkout for an international destination — that would route the order through the wrong checkout flow and carries tax / regulatory risk. |
| Handoff fails (Global-e API outage at cart → handoff)                      | Surface a hard error: "International checkout is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly." Do not place the order in SFCC.                                                                                                                                                   |
| Return webhook from Global-e to SFCC is delayed                            | Render the confirmation with the order reference and a "Your order is being processed" state. Full details render once SFCC receives the order.                                                                                                                                        |
| Cart total mismatch between SFCC and Global-e at handoff                   | Reject the order; surface a hard error. Never silently adjust totals.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## 8. Security

- The Global-e checkout domain is third-party. Cross-site cookies do not propagate — cart context is passed inside the handoff payload, not via cookies.
- The `postMessage` listener in the parent frame must enforce all three checks documented in §3 — `event.origin`, `event.source`, and message schema — plus `orderRef` format validation and URL-safe query encoding before constructing the confirmation URL. See §3 "Return path" for the full requirements.

## 9. Open items

1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply:

   - The `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers.
   - The `postMessage` trusted sender origin — the vendor guide confirms that the Global-e iframe sends a `postMessage` to the parent frame to trigger `orderCreate()`, but does not specify the exact origin string or the full message schema. The `event.origin` value and message payload shape must be obtained from Global-e directly before the listener can be safely implemented.
     Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.

2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order (from SFCC), to decide between full order detail and a "View on tracking page" fallback.
   Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Byte-for-byte SVG path-data parity check between committed source SVGs and the
inlined JSX in zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx. Uses a real XML parser
(xml.etree.ElementTree) for the .svg files. The .tsx side is not XML, so it is
extracted with a carefully bounded regex (balanced-quote aware), then compared
character-for-character.
"""
import re
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

REPO = "/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa"
SVG_NS = "{http://www.w3.org/2000/svg}"

APPLE_SVG = f"{REPO}/overrides/app/assets/svg/apple-pay-logo.svg"
GOOGLE_SVG = f"{REPO}/overrides/app/assets/svg/google-pay-logo.svg"
TSX = f"{REPO}/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx"


def parse_svg(path):
    tree = ET.parse(path)
    root = tree.getroot()
    root_attrs = {
        "viewBox": root.get("viewBox"),
        "width": root.get("width"),
        "height": root.get("height"),
        "preserveAspectRatio": root.get("preserveAspectRatio"),
    }
    paths = []
    # iter() walks in document order, depth-first — exactly the order a renderer
    # (and a human reading top-to-bottom) would encounter them, regardless of
    # nesting inside <g> groups.
    for el in root.iter(f"{SVG_NS}path"):
        paths.append({"id": el.get("id"), "d": el.get("d")})
    return {"root": root_attrs, "paths": paths}


def extract_svg_blocks_from_tsx(tsx_source):
    """
    Returns a dict: {"ApplePayMark": {...}, "GooglePayMark": {...}} each with
    root attrs (viewBox/width/height/preserveAspectRatio-if-present) and an
    ordered list of {"d": ...} dicts, extracted from that component's own
    <chakra.svg>...</chakra.svg> block only (bounded so we can't accidentally
    bleed into a sibling component).
    """
    results = {}
    # Bound each component to its own const ... = () => { ... }; block by
    # locating the next top-level "const XxxMark = ()" or end of a known
    # marker, using the actual function bodies which end with "};" on its own
    # line at column 0 in this file (verified by manual read of the file).
    component_pattern = re.compile(
        r"const (ApplePayMark|GooglePayMark) = \(\) => \{(?P<body>.*?)\n\};", re.DOTALL
    )
    for m in component_pattern.finditer(tsx_source):
        name = m.group(1)
        body = m.group("body")

        svg_open_match = re.search(r"<chakra\.svg(?P<attrs>.*?)>", body, re.DOTALL)
        if not svg_open_match:
            raise ValueError(f"{name}: could not find <chakra.svg ...> opening tag")
        attrs_blob = svg_open_match.group("attrs")

        def grab_attr(attr_name, blob=attrs_blob):
            # Matches attr="value" allowing the value to contain anything except an
            # unescaped double-quote (none of our target attrs need escaping).
            am = re.search(attr_name + r'="([^"]*)"', blob)
            return am.group(1) if am else None

        root_attrs = {
            "viewBox": grab_attr("viewBox"),
            "width": grab_attr("width"),
            "height": grab_attr("height"),
            "preserveAspectRatio": grab_attr("preserveAspectRatio"),
        }

        # Extract every `d="..."` in this component's body, in document order.
        # Use a non-greedy match up to the first unescaped closing quote. SVG path
        # data never legitimately contains a literal double-quote character, so
        # "first closing quote" is unambiguous here — but we still sanity check
        # length below against a manual line-count/char-count pass.
        d_matches = re.findall(r'd="([^"]*)"', body)
        paths = [{"d": d} for d in d_matches]

        results[name] = {"root": root_attrs, "paths": paths}
    return results


def compare_strings(label, a, b):
    if a == b:
        return True, f"PASS — {label}: exact match, length {len(a)} chars"
    # Find first differing index
    min_len = min(len(a), len(b))
    first_diff = None
    for i in range(min_len):
        if a[i] != b[i]:
            first_diff = i
            break
    if first_diff is None:
        first_diff = min_len  # one is a prefix of the other
    start = max(0, first_diff - 20)
    end_a = min(len(a), first_diff + 20)
    end_b = min(len(b), first_diff + 20)
    ctx_a = a[start:end_a]
    ctx_b = b[start:end_b]
    return False, (
        f"FAIL — {label}: lengths {len(a)} vs {len(b)}, first differing index {first_diff}\n"
        f"    SOURCE  context: ...{ctx_a}...\n"
        f"    INLINED context: ...{ctx_b}..."
    )


def main():
    apple_src = parse_svg(APPLE_SVG)
    google_src = parse_svg(GOOGLE_SVG)

    tsx_source = open(TSX, encoding="utf-8").read()
    tsx_blocks = extract_svg_blocks_from_tsx(tsx_source)

    report_lines = []

    # --- Sanity check: manual char-count cross-check for each captured `d` ---
    # Re-extract using a completely different technique (split on `d="` then on
    # the next `"`) and confirm identical results to the regex extraction above,
    # so a subtly wrong regex can't silently under/over-capture.
    def manual_extract_ds(body):
        out = []
        idx = 0
        while True:
            start = body.find('d="', idx)
            if start == -1:
                break
            start += len('d="')
            end = body.find('"', start)
            out.append(body[start:end])
            idx = end + 1
        return out

    for name in ("ApplePayMark", "GooglePayMark"):
        comp_pattern = re.compile(
            r"const " + name + r" = \(\) => \{(?P<body>.*?)\n\};", re.DOTALL
        )
        m = comp_pattern.search(tsx_source)
        manual_ds = manual_extract_ds(m.group("body"))
        regex_ds = [p["d"] for p in tsx_blocks[name]["paths"]]
        assert manual_ds == regex_ds, (
            f"Sanity check FAILED for {name}: manual extraction disagrees with regex "
            f"extraction — {len(manual_ds)} vs {len(regex_ds)} paths, or content differs."

SFCC-11 step 5.1 (ZimmCartButtonGroup) — Tester report: AC verification, SVG parity, decision-log claims.

=== TASK A — Pass-criterion verification (file:line evidence) ===

**1. Domestic: exactly three children, fixed order.** 🔵 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM.
`index.test.tsx:68-73` — `buttons.toHaveLength(3)` AND `buttons.map(b=>b.textContent)).toEqual([CHECKOUT_NAME, APPLE_PAY_NAME, GOOGLE_PAY_NAME])`. Matches component source order: Checkout (`index.tsx:198-203`) then Apple/Google fragment (`204-229`, Apple before Google). Fully met.

**2. International: exactly ONE child; height claim.** 🔵 CONFIRMED (DOM half) / 🔵 disclosed-proxy (height half), UNIFORM.
DOM half fully met: `index.test.tsx:103-110` — `toHaveLength(1)`, `queryByRole('button',{name:/apple pay/i})).toBeNull()` and same for google pay — uses `.toBeNull()`, not `.not.toBeVisible()`, exactly as required.
Height half: **this is a source-read proxy, not a live measurement.** `index.test.tsx:136-153` only inspects `ZimmCartButtonGroupRecipe.baseStyle` as a plain object and asserts it has no `height`/`minHeight` key plus `display:flex`/`flexDirection:column`. It never renders both variants and diffs actual resolved DOM height. This is exactly the "recipe has no fixed height key" proxy the brief anticipated — criterion partially met by Vitest, live half correctly deferred to the Playwright tester, per the recipe's own comment at `zimmCartButtonGroup.css.ts:16-21` which frames the no-height decision as an inference from flexbox behaviour, not a measured fact.

**3. Checkout button five states (primary).** 🔵 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM.
Source: `zimmButton.css.ts:50-66` (primary: `bg`/`color` default; `_hover`, `_active`, `_disabled` each with a different `bg`; no own `_focusVisible`) + baseStyle `_focusVisible` at `zimmButton.css.ts:41-45` (outline set, vs. primary's own `outline` undefined at rest → focus-visible ≠ default, confirmed). Test: `index.test.tsx:156-207` mirrors this exactly, including deliberately reading `base._focusVisible` rather than `primary._focusVisible` for this variant (correct, since primary declares none of its own). All five states independently confirmed present and distinct in source, not just asserted by the test.

**4. Apple Pay / Google Pay five states (secondary).** 🔵 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM.
Source: `zimmButton.css.ts:91-121` — default (`bg:transparent`, `borderColor`), `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled` each genuinely different, own explicit `_focusVisible` (`116-120`, distinct offset for the 1px border). Test: `index.test.tsx:209-231`. Matches exactly.

**5. Error-in-cart: all three enabled, zero feedback copy.** 🔵 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM.
`index.test.tsx:286-294` — none of 3 buttons `.toBeDisabled()` or `aria-disabled=true`. `index.test.tsx:296-299` — `container.textContent` asserted to equal **exactly** the three button labels concatenated, nothing else — this is a direct, strong assertion (would fail if any stray error/feedback text node existed anywhere in the subtree), not a proxy. `index.stories.tsx:55-73` `ErrorInCart` story is intentionally identical to `Default`, with a comment explaining why. Fully met.

**6. Domestic/international × both auth states → correct navigation.** 🟡 PLAUSIBLE-BUT-IMPRECISE, UNIFORM. This is the one real test-suite quality gap in Task A.
Confirmed literally, by reading the test bodies: the "unauthenticated shopper" (`index.test.tsx:81-86`) and "authenticated shopper" (`88-95`) domestic tests are **mechanically identical** — same render, same click, same assertion — differing only in their title string and an inline comment. Same shape for the international pair (`112-116` vs `118-124`). The component genuinely has no auth-observing input at all (confirmed by full read of `index.tsx` — no `useCurrentCustomer`/customer-type call anywhere; `checkoutOwner`/`navigate` are its only two hook calls). This is **honestly disclosed**, not hidden: `index.test.tsx:88-91` and `118-120` both say outright "this component takes no auth-state prop at all... both auth states exercise the identical code path."
Verdict on defensibility: for **domestic**, fully defensible — the AC's own required outcome doesn't vary by auth status (session-notes.md:508 "domestic, any auth status → straight to checkout"), so proving the single code path twice adds nothing but also claims nothing false. For **international**, also currently defensible **only because the plan's own text explicitly sanctions the stub-for-both-states interim behaviour** (component docblock `index.tsx:41-54`, session-notes.md:520-522: "Leaving international on the base `/checkout` path is the current behaviour... so the stub is a no-op, not a regression"). So this isn't an undisclosed shortcut — but the test **suite's naming still overstates what was verified**: a reader trusting test titles alone (not the inline comments) would credit this suite with exercising two different auth states, when mechanically only one code path was ever run, twice. Recommend collapsing each pair into a single test with a comment, once this is revisited — not a functional defect, a coverage-accounting precision issue.

**7. countries.ts unmodified.** 🔵 CONFIRMED.
Ran `git status --porcelain -- overrides/app/config/countries.ts` myself — **output was empty** (no changes). Confirms Tier 1 file was not touched.

**8. Story title.** 🔵 CONFIRMED.
`index.stories.tsx:17` — `title: 'Commerce/ZimmCartButtonGroup',` — exact match.

**9. Pay marks exist and are used as inlined vector data.** 🔵 CONFIRMED.
Both files present as new/untracked in git status (`overrides/app/assets/svg/apple-pay-logo.svg`, `google-pay-logo.svg`). Task B (below) proves the inlined JSX path data is byte-for-byte identical to these files, confirming genuine use, not just presence.

=== TASK B — SVG byte-for-byte parity (real parser: Python xml.etree.ElementTree) ===

Script: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/6017b702-06fb-4295-9164-1c708495531a/scratchpad/svg_parity_check.py` (scratchpad only, not left in repo). Used `ET.parse` + namespace-qualified `root.iter('{http://www.w3.org/2000/svg}path')` for the two source SVGs (document-order, nesting-agnostic traversal — required for Google Pay's `<g id="Group">`-nested paths). For the `.tsx` side, extracted each component's own `const XxxMark = () => { ... };` body via regex, then pulled every `d="..."` in it — **independently cross-checked with a second, completely different extraction method** (manual `str.find` scanning for `d="`/closing `"`) to guard against a truncated/miscounted capture; both methods agreed exactly on count and content for both components before any comparison ran.

Results, all PASS:
- **Apple Pay**: 1 path (id `Vector`). `d` exact match, **1957/1957 chars**, zero differing characters.
- **Google Pay**: 4 paths, source document order `Vector → Vector_2 → Vector_3 → Vector_4` (confirmed `Vector`/`Vector_2`/`Vector_3` nested inside `<g id="Group">`, `Vector_4` a sibling `<path>` after that group, per `.iter()`'s depth-first walk). Inlined JSX order matches this real document order exactly (not just "same 4 paths, any order"). Exact matches: 127/127, 1004/1004, 483/483, 3057/3057 chars — zero differing characters in any of the four.
- **viewBox**: exact string match both — `"0 0 48 24"` (Apple), `"0 0 45.1717 18"` (Google).

Two real, non-`d` deltas found (in scope per your Task B step 5 ask, though outside the code's own "verbatim" claim, which is scoped only to `d` data + order — see `index.tsx:91-92`'s comment):
- 🔵 **width/height**: Apple source `48`/`24` (unitless) vs inlined `48px`/`24px` — numerically identical, just JSX unit-suffix convention, not a real discrepancy. Google source `45.1717`/`18` vs inlined `45px`/`18px` — a **deliberate, disclosed** rounding (`index.tsx:37` comment: "native 45.1717, rounded per plan.md step 5.1"), matching plan.md's own text verbatim. Not a defect.
- 🔵 **preserveAspectRatio**: both source SVGs carry `preserveAspectRatio="none"` (confirmed by direct file read — line 1 of each). **Neither inlined `<chakra.svg>` sets this attribute at all** (`index.tsx` ApplePayMark `72-79` / GooglePayMark `97-104` — no `preserveAspectRatio` prop). This is a real, previously-undocumented delta from the source files. Assessed as functionally inert today: since each mark is rendered at its own self-consistent native `width`/`height`/`viewBox` (not force-fit into a mismatched box — that's what the `PayMarkSlot` wrapper at `index.tsx:134-145` is for instead), the default `xMidYMid meet` behaviour produces no visible distortion either way. Worth a one-line fix for true source fidelity, but not a live bug. ONE-OFF (same single omission pattern in both marks, not two independent defects).

=== TASK C — Decision-log claims ===

**C1 — `useNavigation()` called directly from a `ui-kits/` leaf.** 🔵 CONFIRMED.
`zimmSearchInput/index.tsx:8` imports it, `:40` calls `const navigate = useNavigation();` directly inside the component body — no prop indirection, called from an atom leaf exactly as the docblock claims.

**C3 — `useExpressCheckoutEnabled()` is a different, non-overlapping axis.** 🔵 CONFIRMED.
Read `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-sf-payments.js:140-150` directly: returns `{pdp, miniCart, cart, checkout}` booleans, gated by `useSFPaymentsEnabled()` (`109-113`: local config AND `useShopperConfiguration('SalesforcePaymentsAllowed')`) intersected with a `expressOnCheckoutPagesEnabled` shopper-configuration array (per-page enablement). This is genuinely orthogonal to region/`checkoutOwner` — no overlap. Matches decision-log item 4 exactly.

**C2 — the 'hybrid'/domestic-market grouping. 🔴 CONFIRMED, this is the most important finding, not a hedge.**

The `CheckoutOwner` doc comment (`countries.ts:26-31`) and **two independent PRD/integration docs** describe a **dynamic, per-shopper** condition, not a static per-site one:
- `.docs/prd/regional.md:86`: "Global-e owns checkout for HK... ME... — **and for any domestic storefront when the customer's selected shipping destination is outside the domestic market**."
- `.docs/integration/08-global-e.md:5`: "When **the shopper's destination** is outside the domestic market of the active storefront, the PWA hands the cart to a Global-e-hosted checkout."

`useCountryConfig()` (`useCountryConfig.ts:18-24`) is confirmed, by direct read, to be **purely static**: it matches only on `site.sfccSiteId` + `locale.id` and has no parameter or code path that can observe an individual shopper's chosen/entered shipping address. So your hypothesis is correct and I independently confirm it: **no version of this component, using only `useCountryConfig()`, could ever implement "hide express buttons only when a US shopper is shipping internationally"** — it can only render identically for every US-domestic-site shopper regardless of their real destination, under any interpretation of the doc comment.

Full codebase/doc sweep (not just spot checks) for a countervailing mechanism, all negative:
- Grepped `overrides/`, `.docs/`, and `.claude/session-notes.md` for `hybrid`, `shipping destination`, `domestic market`, `globalEPricing` — the only code reference to `'hybrid'` besides this component's own decision log is the `countries.ts` type/data itself; no other component branches on it.
- Grepped for any "country selector" / "ship to" component anywhere in `overrides/` — **zero results.** `.docs/integration/08-global-e.md:104` and `.docs/prd/regional.md:69` both reference "the country selector pre-checkout" (REG-028) as the mechanism that would lock a shopper's shipping country — but this UI component **does not exist yet anywhere in the codebase.**
- Searched `.claude/session-notes.md`'s SFCC-275 write-up (§entries at lines 503-533) and cross-story notes (SFCC-309/383/384, lines 523-533, 580) — these explicitly scope the "region-based hide" to `checkoutOwner` alone, and scope 309/383/384 to "device and browser eligibility, payment flows, tokenisation and order placement" — **nothing anywhere connects "hybrid site + not-yet-built country selector + dynamic Global-e handoff" as a tracked, scoped piece of work.** This is a genuinely new, unflagged gap, not a rehash of a known one.

**A second, compounding discovery not asked for directly but directly relevant:** `.docs/integration/08-global-e.md:23`'s own checkout-ownership matrix states the `/en-ca/` (US international) row is "**same SFCC site**" as `/us/`, "Global-e (REG-005, **branched by shipping address**)" — i.e. this doc itself describes exactly the dynamic single-site mechanism in question. This **directly contradicts** `.docs/prd/regional.md:11` and `.docs/memory/projectState.md:100`, both of which state REG-005 was updated 2026-07-10 to **two separate SFCC sites** (US domestic `/us/`, US international `/en-ca/` under a new site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl`), explicitly "supersed[ing] the 2026-06-11 single-site decision." The actual code agrees with the two-site version: `countries.ts:69-73`'s own comment says `'en-ca'` "has no matching entry in countries.generated.ts yet... excluded... until the ZimmermannUSIntl site is added." So `08-global-e.md`'s matrix row is very likely stale (not yet updated after the 2026-07-10 revision) — but nothing in the repo says so explicitly, and this component's decision log doesn't reference `08-global-e.md`, REG-005, or the site-split rationale at all. It justifies grouping `'hybrid'` with `'sfcc'` purely by `globalEPricing: false` matching (`index.tsx:245-254`), which is circumstantial, not the authoritative reasoning — and happens to land on a plausible-but-uncited outcome (if the site-split is what actually resolves this, treating `'hybrid'` as domestic-for-now is directionally reasonable) without ever surfacing that the doc comment it's implicitly reinterpreting is either stale or describes something architecturally impossible today.

**Severity verdict: 🔴, CONFIRMED, not a hedge.** The decision log's self-description — "not a direct quote from the doc comment... my own inference" — materially understates the real situation on two counts: (1) it doesn't disclose that the doc comment's literal claim is currently **impossible to implement** with this component's only data source, for any hybrid site, under any reading; (2) it doesn't disclose the live, unreconciled `08-global-e.md` vs. `regional.md`/`projectState.md` conflict about whether `'hybrid'` even still needs dynamic behaviour post-site-split. This should go back to Marcel/product as a named doc-conflict-plus-architecture-gap requiring an explicit decision (and a doc fix to whichever of `08-global-e.md`'s matrix or `countries.ts`'s type comment is stale) — not something this component (or this Tester) should resolve by inference. ONE-OFF today (no other component yet branches on `checkoutOwner==='hybrid'` distinctly), but the `CheckoutOwner` field's own doc comment at `countries.ts:46-49` ("Branch checkout AND pricing logic from this field at PDP/cart level — not only at the checkout page") means every future PDP/cart component that reads `checkoutOwner` will hit this exact same ambiguity — so treat it as latently UNIFORM/systemic, not contained to this one component.

=== What I could not verify, and why ===
- Live resolved-height comparison for AC2 (domestic vs. international) — requires a real browser; explicitly out of my lane, owned by the Playwright/live-rendering tester.
- Whether `npm run test`/`vitest` actually pass when executed — I verified every assertion's target values against the real source files by hand instead of running the suite, since tsc/vitest/audit:tokens execution is explicitly the other tester's lane. I'm confident the assertions are backed by real, matching source values (cited above), but did not execute the runner myself.
- Live Figma comparison (node 9323:95939) for the icon-only visual fix claimed in decision-log item 3 — no Figma access invoked in this task; out of my lane (styling-conformance / live-rendering testers).
- Whether CODEOWNERS/tier routing for the two new `.svg` assets and the new molecule folder is correct — not asked, and adjacent to the structure/DRY tester's lane.

Used `ET.parse` + namespace-qualified `root.iter('{http://www.w3.org/2000/svg}path')` for the two source SVGs (document-order, nesting-agnostic traversal — required for Google Pay's `<g id="Group">`-nested paths). For the `.tsx` side, extracted each component's own `const XxxMark = () => { ... };` body via regex, then pulled every `d="..."` in it — **independently cross-checked with a second, completely different extraction method** (manual `str.find` scanning for `d="`/closing `"`) to guard against a truncated/miscounted capture; both methods agreed exactly on count and content for both components before any comparison ran.

Results, all PASS:
- **Apple Pay**: 1 path (id `Vector`). `d` exact match, **1957/1957 chars**, zero differing characters.
- **Google Pay**: 4 paths, source document order `Vector → Vector_2 → Vector_3 → Vector_4` (confirmed `Vector`/`Vector_2`/`Vector_3` nested inside `<g id="Group">`, `Vector_4` a sibling `<path>` after that group, per `.iter()`'s depth-first walk). Inlined JSX order matches this real document order exactly (not just "same 4 paths, any order"). Exact matches: 127/127, 1004/1004, 483/483, 3057/3057 chars — zero differing characters in any of the four.
- **viewBox**: exact string match both — `"0 0 48 24"` (Apple), `"0 0 45.1717 18"` (Google).

Two real, non-`d` deltas found (in scope per your Task B step 5 ask, though outside the code's own "verbatim" claim, which is scoped only to `d` data + order — see `index.tsx:91-92`'s comment):
- 🔵 **width/height**: Apple source `48`/`24` (unitless) vs inlined `48px`/`24px` — numerically identical, just JSX unit-suffix convention, not a real discrepancy. Google source `45.1717`/`18` vs inlined `45px`/`18px` — a **deliberate, disclosed** rounding (`index.tsx:37` comment: "native 45.1717, rounded per plan.md step 5.1"), matching plan.md's own text verbatim. Not a defect.
- 🔵 **preserveAspectRatio**: both source SVGs carry `preserveAspectRatio="none"` (confirmed by direct file read — line 1 of each). **Neither inlined `<chakra.svg>` sets this attribute at all** (`index.tsx` ApplePayMark `72-79` / GooglePayMark `97-104` — no `preserveAspectRatio` prop). This is a real, previously-undocumented delta from the source files. Assessed as functionally inert today: since each mark is rendered at its own self-consistent native `width`/`height`/`viewBox` (not force-fit into a mismatched box — that's what the `PayMarkSlot` wrapper at `index.tsx:134-145` is for instead), the default `xMidYMid meet` behaviour produces no visible distortion either way. Worth a one-line fix for true source fidelity, but not a live bug. ONE-OFF (same single omission pattern in both marks, not two independent defects).

=== TASK C — Decision-log claims ===

**C1 — `useNavigation()` called directly from a `ui-kits/` leaf.** 🔵 CONFIRMED.
`zimmSearchInput/index.tsx:8` imports it, `:40` calls `const navigate = useNavigation();` directly inside the component body — no prop indirection, called from an atom leaf exactly as the docblock claims.

**C3 — `useExpressCheckoutEnabled()` is a different, non-overlapping axis.** 🔵 CONFIRMED.
Read `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-sf-payments.js:140-150` directly: returns `{pdp, miniCart, cart, checkout}` booleans, gated by `useSFPaymentsEnabled()` (`109-113`: local config AND `useShopperConfiguration('SalesforcePaymentsAllowed')`) intersected with a `expressOnCheckoutPagesEnabled` shopper-configuration array (per-page enablement). This is genuinely orthogonal to region/`checkoutOwner` — no overlap. Matches decision-log item 4 exactly.

**C2 — the 'hybrid'/domestic-market grouping. 🔴 CONFIRMED, this is the most important finding, not a hedge.**

The `CheckoutOwner` doc comment (`countries.ts:26-31`) and **two independent PRD/integration docs** describe a **dynamic, per-shopper** condition, not a static per-site one:
- `.docs/prd/regional.md:86`: "Global-e owns checkout for HK... ME... — **and for any domestic storefront when the customer's selected shipping destination is outside the domestic market**."
- `.docs/integration/08-global-e.md:5`: "When **the shopper's destination** is outside the domestic market of the active storefront, the PWA hands the cart to a Global-e-hosted checkout."

`useCountryConfig()` (`useCountryConfig.ts:18-24`) is confirmed, by direct read, to be **purely static**: it matches only on `site.sfccSiteId` + `locale.id` and has no parameter or code path that can observe an individual shopper's chosen/entered shipping address. So your hypothesis is correct and I independently confirm it: **no version of this component, using only `useCountryConfig()`, could ever implement "hide express buttons only when a US shopper is shipping internationally"** — it can only render identically for every US-domestic-site shopper regardless of their real destination, under any interpretation of the doc comment.

Full codebase/doc sweep (not just spot checks) for a countervailing mechanism, all negative:
- Grepped `overrides/`, `.docs/`, and `.claude/session-notes.md` for `hybrid`, `shipping destination`, `domestic market`, `globalEPricing` — the only code reference to `'hybrid'` besides this component's own decision log is the `countries.ts` type/data itself; no other component branches on it.
- Grepped for any "country selector" / "ship to" component anywhere in `overrides/` — **zero results.** `.docs/integration/08-global-e.md:104` and `.docs/prd/regional.md:69` both reference "the country selector pre-checkout" (REG-028) as the mechanism that would lock a shopper's shipping country — but this UI component **does not exist yet anywhere in the codebase.**
- Searched `.claude/session-notes.md`'s SFCC-275 write-up (§entries at lines 503-533) and cross-story notes (SFCC-309/383/384, lines 523-533, 580) — these explicitly scope the "region-based hide" to `checkoutOwner` alone, and scope 309/383/384 to "device and browser eligibility, payment flows, tokenisation and order placement" — **nothing anywhere connects "hybrid site + not-yet-built country selector + dynamic Global-e handoff" as a tracked, scoped piece of work.** This is a genuinely new, unflagged gap, not a rehash of a known one.

**A second, compounding discovery not asked for directly but directly relevant:** `.docs/integration/08-global-e.md:23`'s own checkout-ownership matrix states the `/en-ca/` (US international) row is "**same SFCC site**" as `/us/`, "Global-e (REG-005, **branched by shipping address**)" — i.e. this doc itself describes exactly the dynamic single-site mechanism in question. This **directly contradicts** `.docs/prd/regional.md:11` and `.docs/memory/projectState.md:100`, both of which state REG-005 was updated 2026-07-10 to **two separate SFCC sites** (US domestic `/us/`, US international `/en-ca/` under a new site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl`), explicitly "supersed[ing] the 2026-06-11 single-site decision." The actual code agrees with the two-site version: `countries.ts:69-73`'s own comment says `'en-ca'` "has no matching entry in countries.generated.ts yet... excluded... until the ZimmermannUSIntl site is added." So `08-global-e.md`'s matrix row is very likely stale (not yet updated after the 2026-07-10 revision) — but nothing in the repo says so explicitly, and this component's decision log doesn't reference `08-global-e.md`, REG-005, or the site-split rationale at all. It justifies grouping `'hybrid'` with `'sfcc'` purely by `globalEPricing: false` matching (`index.tsx:245-254`), which is circumstantial, not the authoritative reasoning — and happens to land on a plausible-but-uncited outcome (if the site-split is what actually resolves this, treating `'hybrid'` as domestic-for-now is directionally reasonable) without ever surfacing that the doc comment it's implicitly reinterpreting is either stale or describes something architecturally impossible today.

**Severity verdict: 🔴, CONFIRMED, not a hedge.** The decision log's self-description — "not a direct quote from the doc comment... my own inference" — materially understates the real situation on two counts: (1) it doesn't disclose that the doc comment's literal claim is currently **impossible to implement** with this component's only data source, for any hybrid site, under any reading; (2) it doesn't disclose the live, unreconciled `08-global-e.md` vs. `regional.md`/`projectState.md` conflict about whether `'hybrid'` even still needs dynamic behaviour post-site-split. This should go back to Marcel/product as a named doc-conflict-plus-architecture-gap requiring an explicit decision (and a doc fix to whichever of `08-global-e.md`'s matrix or `countries.ts`'s type comment is stale) — not something this component (or this Tester) should resolve by inference. ONE-OFF today (no other component yet branches on `checkoutOwner==='hybrid'` distinctly), but the `CheckoutOwner` field's own doc comment at `countries.ts:46-49` ("Branch checkout AND pricing logic from this field at PDP/cart level — not only at the checkout page") means every future PDP/cart component that reads `checkoutOwner` will hit this exact same ambiguity — so treat it as latently UNIFORM/systemic, not contained to this one component.

=== What I could not verify, and why ===
- Live resolved-height comparison for AC2 (domestic vs. international) — requires a real browser; explicitly out of my lane, owned by the Playwright/live-rendering tester.
- Whether `npm run test`/`vitest` actually pass when executed — I verified every assertion's target values against the real source files by hand instead of running the suite, since tsc/vitest/audit:tokens execution is explicitly the other tester's lane. I'm confident the assertions are backed by real, matching source values (cited above), but did not execute the runner myself.
- Live Figma comparison (node 9323:95939) for the icon-only visual fix claimed in decision-log item 3 — no Figma access invoked in this task; out of my lane (styling-conformance / live-rendering testers).
- Whether CODEOWNERS/tier routing for the two new `.svg` assets and the new molecule folder is correct — not asked, and adjacent to the structure/DRY tester's lane.
